extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy Voting & Professional Members, media companies, producers, engineers, artists and submitters preparing GRAMMY entries
extracted.subtask_description: Official Recording Academy rules describing eligibility, submission procedures, category-specific judging criteria, nominee/statuette entitlement, screening and voting processes, entry fees, product/streaming requirements, and credit-change/challenge procedures for GRAMMY Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Engineered Album, Classical — primary judging criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic criterion for judging should be the finished product; that is, the commercially released recording itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, the overall mix, any unique techniques, the quality of sound, and the trueness of its reproduction are considered. Other factors, such as overdubbing or the number of tracks used or the site or mode of the recordings, are secondary. Any appraisal of a recording should be made on the basis of the total album itself. Nominees are Engineers (see P&E list for eligible credits) & Mastering Engineer. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Engineers & Mastering Engineer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Of The Year, Classical — body-of-work eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: This Category is for a producer whose body of work released for the first time during the eligibility year represents consistently outstanding creativity in recording production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One album is required to qualify. The body of work will be up to nine projects; if more than nine entries are submitted, the producer selects which nine to include. Minimum qualifications may be satisfied by combining solo and team credits; an individual may enter solo and co-production recordings, but a producer team must enter only projects worked on as a team. An individual cannot appear on the ballot as both an individual and a member of a producer team. Only recordings released in the current eligibility year are eligible; tracks from albums released in a previous year are not eligible even if released as a single. Reissued and historical recordings are not eligible. Nominees are Producer(s). GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Producer(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Immersive Audio Album — format and mix originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in multichannel immersive audio recordings; eligible recordings must be commercially released on a consumer format/configuration that provides an original immersive mix of four or more channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible consumer formats include DVD-Video, DVD-Audio, SACD, Blu-ray, Atmos, Auro-3D, immersive download, etc. The mix must be an original immersive mix (not electronically repurposed). On releases with multiple distinct mixes, entrants must choose which immersive mix they are entering; only one mix per album will be eligible. Nominees are Immersive Audio Engineer(s)/Mixer(s), Immersive Audio Producer(s) & Immersive Audio Mastering Engineer(s), if applicable. If album is released only in multichannel format, the Producer(s) and Engineer(s)/Mixer(s) receive an award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Instrumental Composition — scope of eligible works
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to any original non-classical composition without lyrics first released on a recording during the eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes original instrumental themes or main titles for motion pictures/television, jazz compositions, and new composition backing spoken word entries. Instrumental compositions with “vocal coloring” are eligible. Nominees are Composer(s) of new material; GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Composer(s) of new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Arrangement, Instrumental or A Cappella — definition & eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in instrumental arrangements on instrumental recordings or a cappella arrangements on vocal a cappella recordings; open to singles or tracks from albums released during the current eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An arrangement is the organization of structure, rhythm, melodies, and harmonies for instruments and/or voices into a cohesive performance piece or recording; it can be a development, enhanced adaptation or a considerable reworking of an original composition and may include dynamics, modulations, tempo variations, improvisation, and various textures. Instrumental recordings with “vocal coloring” and vocal arrangements with “instrumental coloring” are eligible. No arranger may be entered more than twice in the same arranging Category for arranging entries accompanying the same artist. Nominees are Arranger(s); GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Arranger(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Arrangement, Instruments and Vocals — definition & eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in arrangements that feature instrumental and vocal performance in any combination; open to singles or tracks from albums released during the current eligibility year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An arrangement is the organization of structure, rhythm, melodies, and harmonies for instruments and/or voices into a cohesive performance piece or recording. An arrangement can be a development, enhanced adaptation or a considerable reworking of an original composition and may include dynamics, modulations, tempo variations, improvisation, and various textures. No arranger may be entered more than twice in the same arranging Category for arranging entries accompanying the same artist. Nominees are Arranger(s); GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Arranger(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical Field — album vs track eligibility rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In classical Categories where both albums and tracks are eligible, if the entire album qualifies as an entry, then tracks from that album are not also eligible in the Category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical tracks (newly recorded) are allowed entry as separate entities regardless of the percentage of playing time of the album and/or other recorded material on the album that may be of a non-classical genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Orchestral Performance — ensemble-size & scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in recordings of classical orchestral performance; recordings that are predominantly orchestral in performance and intent by large ensembles of 25 or more are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordings may include incidental vocal elements. If orchestral works are coupled with a solo or chamber recording, only the orchestral portion is eligible in this Category. Concertos with solo instrumental performances are eligible in Best Classical Instrumental Solo only. The orchestral organization is not considered a nominee, only a statuette winner. Nominees are Conductor. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Conductor, Orchestra/Large Ensemble; Producer(s) & Engineer(s) if other than Artist of >50% playing time; Composer & Librettist/Lyricist eligibility applies if >50% world premiere content and playing time thresholds are met (see guidance). Note: Composer winning Best Contemporary Classical Composition in same year and represented on a recording that wins another Classical category shall not be eligible to receive more than one GRAMMY statuette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Opera Recording — completeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in albums of complete opera recordings; highlights, arias, recital repertoire, and albums extracted from complete operas are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both audio-only and audio-video (DVD) entries are eligible, but for audio-video only the audio portion is considered. Nominees are Conductor, Principal Soloists & Producer(s). GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Conductor, Principal Soloists; Composer(s) & Librettist if each wrote >50% of the music and libretto of the opera (for new recordings of the entire opera).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Choral Performance — ensemble-size & extraction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in recordings of classical choral performance; choral ensembles comprised of 16 or more vocalists are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choral numbers qualify only if recorded as separate productions and not extracted from a complete work. Choral performances extracted from opera or symphonic recordings are not eligible. The choral organization is not considered a nominee, only a statuette winner. Nominees are Conductor, Choral Director & Chorus Master. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Conductor, Choral Director & Chorus Master, Choral Ensemble; Producer(s) & Engineer(s) if other than Artist of >50% playing time; Composer & Librettist eligibility applies under >50% world premiere criteria (see guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Chamber Music/Small Ensemble Performance — size limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in classical chamber music and small ensemble performance recordings; instrumental, vocal or mixed groups are eligible as long as participants do not exceed 24 (not including conductor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choral ensembles comprised of 16 or more vocalists are eligible only in Best Choral Performance. Nominees are Conductor & Ensemble. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Conductor & Ensemble; Producer(s) & Engineer(s) if other than Artist of >50% playing time; Composer & Librettist eligibility applies under >50% world premiere criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Classical Instrumental Solo — scope and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in classical instrumental solo recordings, including concertos and concerto-style works (including multi-instrumental concertos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominees are Instrumental Soloist(s) & Conductor. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Instrumental Soloist & Conductor; Producer(s) & Engineer(s) if other than Artist of >50% playing time; Composer & Librettist eligibility applies under >50% world premiere criteria (see guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Classical Solo Vocal Album — eligible content
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes excellence in albums of classical solo vocal recordings; eligible albums may contain song literature, operatic arias, vocal cycles, and/or other types of vocal music with collaborating artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple soloists are eligible in this Category. Arias qualify only if recorded as separate productions and not extracted from a complete work. Nominees are Vocal Soloist, Pianist, Ensemble(s) & Conductor (if applicable). GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Vocal Soloist; Collaborative Artist(s), Producer(s) & Engineer(s) if other than Artist of >50% playing time; Composer & Librettist eligibility applies under >50% world premiere criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Classical Compendium — unifying concept & crossover rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For an album developed and united by an artist, composer, tribute, thematic idea, musical, or other unifying concept; classical crossover projects and albums with at least 50% playing time intersecting other genres with Classical Music are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Albums may include historic, spoken and/or documentary material if those portions do not exceed 49% total playing time. Albums entered in Classical Compendium may not be entered in other classical Categories, but individual tracks/pieces may be entered in other Categories. Award to the artists, conductors, composers, and producers with 50% or more playing time. Nominees are Artist(s), Conductor(s) & Producer(s) of >50% playing time of the album. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Artist(s) & Producer(s) of >50% playing time; Composer(s) with >50% playing time and sole Librettist/Lyricists if applicable; Recording Engineer(s) and/or Mixer(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Contemporary Classical Composition — originality & score requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to original classical compositions, including newly composed operas, composed within the last 25 years and released on a recording for the first time during the eligibility year; eligible compositions must be individual works and world premiere recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New versions, arrangements, suites, transcriptions, reorchestrations, remixes, and/or any other variants of preexisting compositions are not eligible. The full-length score on PDF must be submitted with each entry for this Category. Nominees are Composer & Librettist. GRAMMY statuettes awarded to Composer & Librettist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make GRAMMY entries (Rule Five)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings are submitted for consideration through the GRAMMY Online Entry Process (OEP). All Voting and Professional Recording Academy Members may make GRAMMY entries. Registered media companies that release qualifying recordings during the eligibility period may also make entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Recording Academy defines a media company as a legitimate business entity whose core business is to create, aggregate and promote audio and/or video content for commercial purposes and that must have verifiable product in national U.S. commercial distribution on approved streaming platforms within the current eligibility period. The Academy reserves the right to remove entries where the submitter is not an individual who would be entitled to receive a nomination and/or a statuette. Media companies must register and be approved before accessing OEP. Entry access dates provided (example for 68th GRAMMYs: July 16 - August 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration fees for media companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Media companies pay an annual fee to register with the Academy that is 20% more than the annual fee paid by individuals for membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fee is $180 for the 68th GRAMMY Awards (example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-entry fee policy & courtesy entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-entry fee structure encourages mindful decisions; all Professional and Voting Members receive five (5) courtesy entries every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any member financially burdened by entry fees can request a waiver by contacting the Awards Department. Fees vary by entry timing (early/standard/final).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-entry fee schedule (timed pricing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry fees vary by submission window: Early Entry Pricing, Standard Pricing, Final Deadline Pricing with different amounts for Members and Media Companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example schedule for specified windows: Members early $40 (after 5 courtesy entries), standard $75, final $125; Media companies early $65, standard $95, final $125. (Amounts and windows shown in published schedule.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry limits in OEP
rubrics_metrics.description: The Online Entry Process is programmed to limit entries in genre categories to one per recording for albums, and limits track/single entries to one for performance categories and one for song/composition categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GRAMMY entries are made for specific recordings: entrants must provide the UPC or ISRC number, upload and confirm full track listing and confirmed final crediting. The entrant affirms that it is that specific recording that should be used by Screening and Craft Committees and voters. Alternate versions/configurations with different UPC/ISRC and different tracks or credits are not considered eligible when they differ from the entered version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming links and physical product requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Academy members and media companies must provide eligible streaming links for each entry (exceptions for certain Craft categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may provide up to five links from different eligible streaming services (artist/label site links do not qualify). Entries will be disqualified if a streaming link is not provided or is incorrect. Product copies required for certain Categories (e.g., Best Album Notes: 1 copy; Best Recording Package: 2 copies; Best Historical Album: 2 copies; Best Immersive Audio Album: 3 copies if not uploaded). Product is due within ten days of submission and all required product must be received by the Academy by the specified deadline (example: September 8). If an entry is made in multiple Craft Categories, additional copies per category must be sent. Physical-release-only entries (sold via artist/label website) may be eligible if meeting specific distribution and accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category screening process and artist intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries in most categories are screened by committees of genre experts to determine appropriate category and field placement; Screening Committee is expected to consider the artist’s intent as part of the decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure whether to move a recording, artist’s intent (as indicated by initial entry category) is the deciding factor. Recordings remain in the initially entered genre absent a supermajority vote (not less than 2/3) by the Screening Committee to move it. Screening Meetings include experts from Chapters nationwide; there is a National Screening Committee for Best New Artist eligibility and unresolved screening issues. A list of genre Screening Committees is provided (e.g., Alternative, Americana, Classical, Pop, Rap/R&B, etc.). Entries in Comedy Album are screened by staff and consulted experts if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination counts & minimum-entry thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of nominations: General Field Categories (Record Of The Year, Song Of The Year, Album Of The Year, Best New Artist) have eight nominations; Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical, and Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical have five; other Categories generally have five nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the event of a tie, there shall be no more than seven and no less than three nominations in these categories. Each category shall have at least 40 distinct artist entries; if a category receives 25–39 entries, only three recordings will receive nominations that year. Fewer than 25 entries -> category goes on hiatus for the year (no award); if fewer than 25 entries for three consecutive years, category will be discontinued and submissions entered into next most appropriate category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination voting scope for Voting Members
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are determined by Voting Members through first round voting or Craft Nominating Committee processes; all Voting Members are encouraged to vote in the six General Field categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, voters may vote in up to 10 other categories on both ballots, and those 10 must be within no more than three fields where the voter is actively engaged as a peer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Nominating Committee membership qualifications and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft Committee members must be Voting Members in the membership class corresponding to the Craft they judge and must provide documentation that they are actively working in the Craft (current released credits within last five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters’ Executive Directors work with Nominating/Executive Committees and Chapter Presidents to develop slates; recommendations can be supplemented by CEO/National Chair for DEI/balance. Final slate ratified by National Board of Trustees. Committee members are solicited for member recommendations. No person serves more than five consecutive years without a break; chairs may serve up to an additional three consecutive years if necessary. Committee members may serve a maximum of eight consecutive years (if served first then elected chair) with two years off to reset. At least 25% of each committee must turn over year-to-year. Each committee votes annually to recommend a Chair for next year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft/committee-specific nomination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Craft Categories use special committee processes to determine nominations, with different committee sizes and procedures depending on the Category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Best Recording Package, Best Album Cover, Best Album Notes, Best Historical Album, Best Immersive Audio Album are voted on by National Craft Nominating Committees (25 Voting Members) to select five nominations (in-person except Best Album Notes which meets virtually). For Best Instrumental Composition; Best Arrangement categories; Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical; and Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical: first round by General Voting Membership, second round by National Craft Nominating Committees from top 30 selections. Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical uses first-round general membership plus Chapter Engineering Committees to create a Selections List; second round by twelve Chapter Craft Committees. Producer of the Year, Classical; Best Engineered Album, Classical; Best Contemporary Classical Composition follow a general-first/committee-second model. Best Music Video/Film: first round by General Voting Membership, second round by National Craft Nominating Committee (16–20 Voting Members balanced in video and film) from top ~30 selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on number of nominations any nominee may receive in one category
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules define how many nominations an individual nominee or artist may receive in a single Category, with different constraints depending on category type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For categories where the Artist is a Nominee: up to two nominations per artist provided at least one is with a co-nominee(s). For categories where the Artist is not a Nominee: up to two nominations per nominee provided the works are by different Artists (or no limit provided works are by different Artists and one is individual and others with different co-nominees). For Body Of Work Categories (Producer Of The Year, Non-Classical; Producer Of The Year, Classical; Songwriter Of The Year, Non-Classical) and Best New Artist: only one nomination per nominee. For Classical Categories: one nomination generally, with exceptions allowing two nominations if orchestra/chorus/co-nominee is different or if principal soloists are different. For Music Video/Music Film categories: one nomination per video or film. 'Works' includes albums, tracks, singles, songs, compositions, arrangements, remixes, packages, album notes, music videos/films, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination change request policy (pre-announcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission period closes and before nominations announcement, submitter may request credit changes with required documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation: affidavit verifying change is true; reason for change; submit updated (final) label copy; confirmation that credits have been updated across DSPs as applicable. Requests must be made through the GRAMMY Credit and Nomination Corrections portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and requirements for credit corrections before the telecast (post-announcement short window)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the nominations announcement, the submitter may request changes in original credits within two weeks after the announcement with specific documentation and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation: formal statement from head of label/content owner/producer detailing inaccuracies and steps to correct; a notarized statement from the artist, where applicable; updated (final) label copy or credit list approved by content owner/producer; call sheets or studio logs proving additional persons worked on recording and their roles, where applicable. There is a fee of $200 per added name to be paid in advance. Confirmation that credits have been updated across DSPs is required. Requests made via the GRAMMY Credit and Nomination Corrections portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for credit corrections after the telecast (one-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual not included in the Final Nominations List who claims a nomination after the deadline will be informed that official changes will be made after the awards telecast; there is a one-year deadline from the telecast to request crediting changes/additions to nominated or winning albums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for after-telecast changes are same as pre-telecast corrections (formal statement, notarized statement where applicable, updated label copy, call sheets/studio logs, $200 per added name, confirmation of DSP updates). After the one-year deadline, requests for changes must be made to the Executive Committee of the Board of Trustees; the requesting party is responsible for providing all necessary documents and it is at the Committee's sole discretion whether to consider the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to GRAMMY Award entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions regarding GRAMMY Award entitlement are made by the Awards Department; any challenge to a final entitlement decision must be made in writing to the Executive Committee of the Recording Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Committee may investigate, consider and decide the challenge and is empowered to act with the power of the Board of Trustees for that purpose. The Executive Committee’s decision is communicated in writing and is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final voting to select GRAMMY winners — confidentiality and tabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: After nominations, the final ballot is made available to all current Voting Members to select winners; all ballots are tabulated confidentially by an independent accounting firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results are not known until the day of the GRAMMY Awards when sealed envelopes with winners' names are delivered by the accounting firm (example: Deloitte).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescindment policy — withdrawn awards
rubrics_metrics.description: If a GRAMMY Award is withdrawn following the presentation, no award is given in that Category for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GRAMMY process does not produce a ranked result with a winner and ordered runners-up; rescindment results in no award for that Category in that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting integrity principle (opening of Rule Nine)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recording Academy aims to ensure the GRAMMY Awards process is fair and ethical and that Voting Members make choices based solely on artistic and technical merits of eligible recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting Members are required to understand and follow guidelines designed to preserve integrity and transparency in the process (further vote solicitation rules and specifics are described in subsequent text).
